title: GP Access Planner
summary: A public-data planning product that forecasts recorded general-practice appointments across England while keeping observed access signals and hypothetical capacity explicitly separate.
outcome: Delivered a source-traceable 7, 14, and 28-day planning surface for 104 sub-ICBs, backed by 32.9 million validated source rows, rolling-origin evaluation, immutable releases, and a live edge API.

deployment.runtime: Static Next.js assets and a TypeScript Worker at the edge

metrics: 32,871,791 source rows loaded with exact-count reconciliation
10.96% 28-day WAPE and 0.580 MASE for the approved seasonal-naive champion
404,772 immutable release files checksum-matched locally and in R2
99.98% smaller metadata response after bounding the serving pointer
stages: Checksum and archive validation for selected public releases
Typed ingestion into immutable PostgreSQL source tables
dbt source-native and derived model construction
Immutable serving-artifact export and R2 verification
Isolated candidate smoke test and pointer-only production promotion
Static planning interface and bounded edge API
architecture: A private build plane validates public source archives and loads PostgreSQL without exposing source credentials to the public runtime.
dbt separates publisher-grain observations from derived marts; forecasting uses only publication-time-safe features.
Python evaluates seasonal naive, Elastic Net, LightGBM, and CatBoost across twelve rolling origins and three horizons.
Approved releases are exported as immutable, checksummed, paged JSON artifacts and uploaded to Cloudflare R2.
A Cloudflare Worker reads a bounded release pointer, applies request limits, and serves versioned envelopes to a static Next.js interface.
Candidate and production Workers use separate pointers; promotion changes only current.json and preserves rollback artifacts.
evaluation: Twelve rolling origins compare one seasonal baseline and three challengers at 7, 14, and 28 days.
A challenger must improve WAPE by at least 5% at every horizon, achieve MASE below 1, and avoid material geography regressions.
Seasonal naive remained champion with 5.60%, 9.10%, and 10.96% WAPE at 7, 14, and 28 days.
The 28-day interval covered 55.09% against a nominal 80% target, so the interface labels the band indicative rather than calibrated.
Release acceptance also checks finite ordered forecasts, exact row reconciliation, checksums, API contracts, and live routes.
operationalTradeoffs: Precomputed forecasts and bounded artifacts remove database credentials and model inference from the public request path, at the cost of batch freshness.
Publisher-grain rows remain traceable, but paged serving indexes add many small immutable objects to each release.
Seasonal naive is less sophisticated than the challengers, but it was the only model that passed every declared promotion gate.
The product forecasts recorded appointments, not slots, utilisation, workload, cancellations, or actual available capacity.
The anonymous portfolio deployment has rate limiting and release rollback but no clinical availability objective.
disclaimer: This public-data portfolio product supports review of recorded appointment pressure only. It contains no PHI, operational slot data, rosters, free text, or clinical advice, and it makes no claim to measure NHS capacity or utilisation.

dataDisclosure.license: Source datasets remain subject to their respective published terms and attribution requirements; this project uses them for a non-commercial portfolio demonstration and implies no NHS endorsement.
dataDisclosure.permittedUse: Non-commercial portfolio review, reproducibility inspection, and planning-method demonstration within each source publisher's terms.

excludedFields: Protected health information, direct identifiers, free text, and patient records
Operational slots, staff rosters, cancellations, workload, and utilisation

Unapproved model outputs and private build-plane state

evidence.method: Twelve rolling origins at 7, 14, and 28 days with WAPE, MASE, interval coverage, and geography regression gates.
evidence.scope: 104 sub-ICBs with twelve months of usable history and at least 90% published GPAD population coverage
evidence.environment: Private PostgreSQL build plane with locked Python dependencies
evidence.caveat: The nominal 80% prediction interval under-covered at 55.09% and is labelled indicative.

evidence.claim: The private snapshot loaded 32,871,791 exact source rows and the dbt build completed every declared node and test.
evidence.method: Checksum and ZIP-CRC validation, typed ingestion, exact row-count reconciliation, and dbt build over PostgreSQL 17.
evidence.result: 32,871,791 rows; 17/17 dbt nodes and tests passed
evidence.classification: public source data with private acquisition metadata
evidence.caveat: Source archives and acquisition records are intentionally excluded from Git.

evidence.claim: The corrected immutable release matched every local and remote object before production promotion.
evidence.method: Manifest validation followed by immutable rclone copy and checksum comparison before writing the candidate pointer.
evidence.result: 404,772 of 404,772 files checksum-matched with zero differences
evidence.caveat: The large object count is the cost of bounded publisher-grain exploration without a public database.

evidence.claim: The anonymous Worker serves the approved release and all product routes after candidate isolation and pointer-only promotion.
evidence.method: Live HTTPS smoke checks over release metadata, 104 geographies, forecasts, observed context, synthetic scenarios, and four product routes.

story.recruiterSummary: Public primary-care data can describe recorded access pressure, but it cannot reveal actual available capacity. GP Access Planner turns that limitation into the product contract: observed appointments and access signals stay separate, forecasts are promoted only through named gates, and visitor-entered capacity remains clearly synthetic. Every headline claim traces to evaluation, release, or live-deployment evidence.
story.technicalNarrative: A private build plane checksum-validates selected public releases, preserves publisher grain in PostgreSQL, and uses dbt to separate source-native observations from derived marts. Python evaluates seasonal naive, Elastic Net, LightGBM, and CatBoost over twelve rolling origins. The baseline remains champion because no challenger passed every horizon and geography gate. The approved snapshot is exported as immutable paged artifacts, checksum-matched into R2, exercised through an isolated candidate Worker, and promoted by changing one bounded pointer. A static Next.js interface consumes versioned API envelopes; scenarios run as deterministic, non-persistent calculations at the edge.
scalabilityRoadmap: Calibrate forecast intervals by geography or pooled cohort before presenting them as probabilistic coverage rather than indicative ranges.
Add automated source-freshness monitoring and a documented release service-level objective before increasing operational reliance.
Measure API latency, cache hit rate, and R2 request cost under representative concurrent browsing before changing the paged artifact design.
Keep capacity schedules synthetic unless governed operational slot and roster data become available with explicit authorization and new disclosure controls.
story.executiveSummary: The live product gives planners a bounded view of where recorded appointment pressure may merit review over the next four weeks. It covers 104 sub-ICBs and keeps context, forecasts, and hypothetical capacity in distinct lanes. The approved baseline remains below the 15% 28-day WAPE ceiling, but interval under-coverage and the absence of operational capacity data are explicit decision limits.
story.intendedUser: A primary-care planning analyst, healthcare analytics reviewer, or hiring manager assessing data contracts, forecast governance, and public-cloud delivery.

example.title: Review four-week recorded appointment pressure without claiming capacity
steps: Select a sub-ICB and inspect the 7, 14, or 28-day recorded-appointment forecast
Read telephone, online, workforce, population, experience, deprivation, and respiratory context as separate signals
Check source coverage, freshness, model version, forecast status, and limitations in the API envelope
Enter a hypothetical weekday schedule in Capacity Lab and compare it with forecast demand
Treat the scenario as synthetic planning evidence, not observed slots, utilisation, workload, or clinical advice

technologyDecisions.rationale: A named baseline makes improvement claims testable and remained the only model to pass every declared horizon and geography gate.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Promote LightGBM or CatBoost on aggregate performance alone
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The simpler model gives up sophistication but avoids promoting a challenger with short-horizon or geography regressions.

technologyDecisions.technology: Immutable R2 artifacts and pointer promotion
technologyDecisions.rationale: Precomputed, checksum-verified objects provide traceability, bounded reads, candidate isolation, and rollback without public database access.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Serve PostgreSQL queries and live model inference
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Batch releases are less fresh and contain many small objects, but the public runtime holds no database credentials.

technologyDecisions.technology: Static Next.js interface with a Worker API
technologyDecisions.rationale: Static product routes keep deployment small while the Worker supplies versioned data envelopes, request limits, and deterministic scenarios.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Run a stateful full-stack application server
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The surface cannot support persistent user accounts or saved scenarios, which matches the anonymous portfolio boundary.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Keeping observed rows at their lowest published grain makes displayed summaries traceable and preserves source nulls and suppression markers.
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Traceability increases artifact volume and requires bounded paging and serving indexes.

evidence.label: 28-day WAPE
evidence.context: Approved seasonal-naive forecast across 104 eligible sub-ICBs and twelve rolling origins.
evidence.method: Weighted absolute percentage error at the longest declared planning horizon.
evidence.meaning: Aggregate error remained below the 15% active-model ceiling.
evidence.threshold: A geography above 15% is held to the prior forecast or historical-only mode.
evidence.interpretation: Evidence for a bounded planning forecast, not a measurement of actual capacity.

evidence.label: Validated source rows
evidence.context: Exact loaded row count across 29 analytical resources in the private build snapshot.
evidence.method: Checksums, archive CRCs, typed ingestion, and row-count reconciliation before dbt modelling.
evidence.meaning: The analysis was built from a reconciled public-data snapshot rather than a small dashboard extract.
evidence.interpretation: Acquisition archives stay private even though the selected source statistics are public.

evidence.label: Checksum-matched release files
evidence.context: Every local object in release 2026-08-13.1 matched its remote R2 counterpart.
evidence.method: Immutable bulk copy followed by manifest-driven remote checksum comparison.
evidence.meaning: The promoted serving release is byte-accounted and rollback-ready.
evidence.interpretation: Integrity evidence does not replace availability or disaster-recovery objectives.

evidence.label: Bounded metadata response
evidence.context: The production metadata response fell from 31,107,910 bytes to 6,134 bytes.
evidence.method: Moved serving metadata into the bounded release pointer while retaining a legacy manifest fallback.
evidence.meaning: The most common API call no longer transfers or parses the full artifact inventory.
evidence.interpretation: A focused response-size optimization; load and latency testing remain future work.

limitations: Recorded appointments are not available slots, workload, utilisation, cancellations, or actual capacity.
The nominal 80% forecast interval achieved 55.09% coverage and is presented only as an indicative range.
No challenger passed every promotion gate, so the approved forecast intentionally remains seasonal naive.
The public snapshot has batch freshness and does not stream operational NHS data.
Synthetic capacity scenarios do not model skill mix, appointment duration, absence, estates, or local booking rules.
The anonymous deployment has no clinical availability objective and must not be used for patient-level or clinical decisions.

bulletCandidates.bullet: Built a public-data GP access planning product across 104 sub-ICBs, reconciling 32.9 million source rows and governing 7, 14, and 28-day forecasts through twelve rolling origins and explicit WAPE, MASE, coverage, and geography gates.

Designed a PostgreSQL and dbt build plane that preserves publisher grain, separates observed and derived measures, and passed 17 of 17 declared nodes and tests before exporting a checksum-verified immutable release.

Delivered a static Next.js and Cloudflare Worker planning surface with bounded versioned APIs, deterministic non-persistent scenarios, candidate isolation, pointer-only promotion, and a 99.98% reduction in release-metadata response size.
